gaps.sentence: You ___ better book now — the prices rise every week.
gaps.explanation: 'Had better' gives strong advice, often with urgency: had better book.

gaps.sentence: He ___ have missed the train — he left home two hours early.
gaps.explanation: 'Can't have' expresses near-certainty that something did not happen: can't have missed.

gaps.sentence: We ___ hurry — the doors close in five minutes.
gaps.explanation: 'Had better' expresses urgent advice: had better hurry.

gaps.sentence: The report ___ to be submitted by noon tomorrow.
gaps.explanation: 'Has to' expresses obligation with a third-person subject: has to be.

gaps.sentence: I really ___ stop drinking so much coffee; the doctor was very clear.
gaps.explanation: 'Must' can express strong obligation the speaker feels: must stop.

gaps.sentence: You ___ have told me earlier — I could have helped.
gaps.explanation: 'Should have told' — reproach about the past.

gaps.sentence: You ___ as well tell him the truth — he will find out anyway.
gaps.explanation: 'Might as well' suggests doing something because there is no reason not to: might as well.

gaps.sentence: I ___ to wear a uniform at my last job, and I hated it.
gaps.hint: an obligation imposed in the past
gaps.explanation: Past obligation is expressed with 'had to': had to wear.
